findings.text: Provides preparation of outbound device transfer storage for a record aware queue, arranging scatter entries for at most the requested payload length starting beyond the record header at the current consumption point.

Requires a positive scatter budget and limits the requested length to a record aware maximum; when remaining queued occupancy cannot hold payload plus header overhead the operation reports no work instead of partial arrangement.
A zero scatter budget triggers a fatal diagnostic rather than returning an error, so callers must guarantee at least one entry before invocation.
Liveness marking uses the least significant bit of the owning container link with numeric value one.
Container recovery mask preserves all address bits of the owning link while clearing the liveness marking bit.
Node to container association shares storage with removal marking; masked interpretation yields the owning container while flag interpretation reports whether logical deletion has occurred.
Associating an already marked node or marking an already marked node emits a diagnostic warning, indicating single lifetime marking is expected.
Fresh association installs the container link in unmarked state, while logical deletion preserves the container bits and sets only the marking bit.
Initializes an empty managed node collection with its serialization guard and optional arrival and final release callbacks.

Node attachment preparation establishes empty linkage, initial reference ownership and container association, then notifies via arrival callback when configured, before linkage becomes visible to others.
Insertion at front or back mutates collection linkage only while holding the owning container guard.
Offers insertion of a newly prepared node at the front or at the rear of a managed collection, combining preparation with guarded linkage.
Supports insertion immediately after or immediately before an existing member, inheriting the container association from the positioned member and guarding the linkage update.
Blocking removal waiter comprises queue linkage for a global wait collection, identity of the target node, identity of the sleeping task, and a wake indicator set by the release path.
Global collection of blocking removal waiters is mutated only while holding a dedicated removal wait guard.
Final reference release unlinks the node from collection linkage, wakes every blocking waiter registered for that node identity, and clears the container association.
Reference release attempt reports whether the release path executed, allowing callers to decide if final release notification remains required.
Logical marking and reference release execute while holding the owning container guard, while the final release callback when needed runs after the guard is released.
Release helper optionally marks the node as removed before dropping a reference, and suppresses the configured release callback unless the drop caused final release.
Provides nonblocking logical deletion that marks a node and releases one reference, leaving physical unlinking until remaining references drain.
Blocking removal entry registers a waiter for the target node, performs logical deletion, then sleeps uninterruptibly until the release path signals completion before restoring running state.
Blocking removal does not time out and cannot be interrupted, so callers must ensure all holders will eventually release or the sleeper never resumes.
Attachment query distinguishes associated nodes from detached ones based on whether the container link has been cleared.
Iterator lifecycle binds an iterator to a collection with empty current, optionally acquiring a live starting node, and later releases any held current without marking.
Acquisition of a starting node for iteration succeeds only for members that have not been fully released, preventing resurrection of drained members.
Linkage to node conversion derives the containing node address from its embedded linkage member.
Bidirectional traversal advances the iterator while skipping logically removed members and maintains exactly one held reference on the returned node when present.

Traversal swaps references and scans for live members while holding the owning container guard with interrupt state preserved, invoking the prior node final callback after guard release when required.
Traversal never returns marked members and yields empty current upon reaching the collection sentinel, releasing the previously held reference in all paths.
Diagnostic formatting for this module prefixes supplied messages with the module name.
Namespace lookup for an object delegates through parent type child operations to a type specific accessor, yielding absence when operations are missing or indicate no namespacing.
Child namespace operations derive solely from the parent type hook when parent and type and hook are all present, otherwise no operations are reported.
Ownership query defaults to global root identity for user and group, delegating to a type specific hook when configured.
Namespace type validity requires a value strictly between the none sentinel and the count sentinel.

Persistent directory establishment guarantees either a fully installed namespaced directory with default attribute groups and a pinned reference surviving ancestor removal, or no residual directory on failure with group installation rolled back.
Enabling namespace filtering during directory creation treats invalid or unregistered child namespace types as fatal diagnostic failures.
Registration query reports whether a namespace type has installed operations, treating out of range types as unregistered.
Namespace registration table inspection holds the dedicated type guard across validity checking and table lookup.
Path length computation accounts for each ancestor name plus a separator and an initial terminator, returning zero when any ancestor lacks a name.
Path materialization writes ancestor names backward from the buffer end with separators and fails when supplied space cannot hold the full hierarchy.
Path accessor allocates a sized buffer for the full ancestor hierarchy and retries allocation on concurrent modification races, returning absence on unnamed ancestors or allocation failure.
Path construction may repeat measurement and allocation when concurrent renaming invalidates the first attempt, so callers must tolerate transient extra allocation.
Set membership linkage changes hold the set list guard, acquiring the set reference before linkage on join and dropping it after unlink on leave.
Set association is a no-op when no set is linked; otherwise join appends the member entry while leave removes and reinitializes it.
Internal initialization establishes reference ownership, empty set linkage, cleared visibility and event flags, and marked initialized state, tolerating an absent handle as a no-op.

Internal registration requires presence and a non-empty name, adopts parent defaulting to the set container when needed, joins the set and creates persistent storage; success leaves the object visible while failure unwinds membership and parent linkage.
Registration with an empty name warns and fails, and name collision in persistent storage produces a distinct diagnostic advising against duplicate names in one directory.

Reference acquisition obtains ownership and returns the same handle while release relinquishes toward final release handling, both tolerating an absent handle as a no-op and warning on uninitialized use.
Naming replaces the stored name with a newly formatted allocation, preserving the existing name when no new format is supplied and reporting allocation failure without altering the old name.

When the formatted name contains path separators they are substituted with a safe character via a mutable copy, ensuring read-only formatted storage is never modified in place and prior storage is released.
Initialization entry validates handle and type presence then establishes internal state and binds the type for later registration.
Initialization with a missing handle or missing type logs an error with diagnostic trace, as does reinitialization of an already initialized object, with the latter still re-establishing state.
Public registration combines formatted naming with internal registration, rejecting absent handles or uninitialized objects with diagnostics.
Combined initialization and registration entry performs type binding followed by named registration under a supplied parent in one call.

Rename exchanges the stored name after a successful namespaced persistent directory rename and emits a move notification carrying the prior full path, releasing all temporaries and the transient reference on every path.

Rename requires a present parented object; directory rename failure leaves the old name intact and propagates the failure, while success swaps names and preserves the old storage only until notification completes.
Move notification exposes the prior full path under a dedicated old path environment variable name.

Event emission entry delivers an action notification for an object with optional caller supplied variables, resolving the owning set by ancestor walk and augmenting with set specific handling and broadcast.

Removal notification is marked as sent regardless of delivery outcome to prevent duplicate automatic cleanup, while addition notification is marked when delivery is attempted and unbind delivery strips alias related variables.
Delivery is silently dropped with success when suppression is set, when the set filter rejects the object, or when subsystem resolution is absent, and fails when no owning set can be resolved.
Emitted environment always carries action identity, full path, subsystem identity and a fresh ordered sequence value, plus caller variables and set specific augmentation when present.
Event emission reports allocation failure for environment storage and path resolution failure distinctly, and propagates augmentation or broadcast failures to the caller.
Helper execution is skipped for objects whose namespace differs from the initial namespace of their type, otherwise helper execution remains eligible.
Helper argument construction appends the subsystem identity into remaining environment buffer space and fails when insufficient room remains.
